steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Beyond Compression Ratio: High-Throughput KV Compression for Disaggregated LLM Serving
summary: The method replaces a multi-stage KV compression pipeline (separate distribution transform, low-bit quantization, and a proprietary lossless backend) with a fused TileLang kernel and an open LC-based compression backend for disaggregated serving. The cost is implementation complexity: it depends on the KVServe disaggregated serving stack, custom TileLang kernels, and the LC library, none of which are drop-in components of standard single-GPU inference frameworks. It can fail when the serving setup is not disaggregated (no KV transfer over a network, so no communication savings to preserve), when interconnect bandwidth is low enough that compression overhead dominates, or when workload-specific KV distributions reduce the achievable compression throughput.
rationale: The technique targets disaggregated multi-node serving with high-bandwidth interconnects, an architecture the reader does not operate on a single 24 GB GPU, so it is worth tracking but not adopting or testing now.
technique: Fused KV compression kernel and high-throughput lossless backend

claims.statement: The method replaces a multi-stage KV compression pipeline (separate distribution transform, low-bit quantization, and a proprietary lossless backend) with a fused TileLang kernel and an open LC-based compression backend for disaggregated serving. The cost is implementation complexity: it depends on the KVServe disaggregated serving stack, custom TileLang kernels, and the LC library, none of which are drop-in components of standard single-GPU inference frameworks. It can fail when the serving setup is not disaggregated (no KV transfer over a network, so no communication savings to preserve), when interconnect bandwidth is low enough that compression overhead dominates, or when workload-specific KV distributions reduce the achievable compression throughput.
The fused kernel achieves up to 5.9x speedup, the lossless backend raises compression throughput from below 90 GB/s to over 500 GB/s, and job completion time is reduced by up to 2.04x.
